chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Murazim, from Muaz ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is from the good fortune of the man that he happens to be the overseer upon his dependants.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a man to be the overseer of his dependants in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith links material provision with spiritual well-being, framing the husband's role as a 'qayyim' (guardian/provider) not merely as a duty but as a source of true 'sa'adah' (happiness). This reflects the Shia emphasis on the family unit as a microcosm of social justice, where the head's stewardship ensures the stability and moral upbringing of dependants.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Murazim, from Moaz Bin Kaseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said,
‘It is from the good fortune of the man that he happens to be the overseer upon his dependants’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Murazim from Mu’adh ibn Kathir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
it is of the prosperity of man to support and provide for his family.”
